mission_requirements.text: The EPS engineering enterprise shall obtain MCR acceptance at the end of Pre-Phase A for a mission concept whose EPS feasibility is justified against agreed stakeholder expectations and mission constraints, supported by initial ConOps, technical budgets, assumptions, risks and a preliminary verification and validation approach.

The enterprise shall obtain SRR acceptance during Phase A for validated EPS requirements and interfaces traced to the mission concept and allocated spacecraft requirements, with measurable criteria consistent with stakeholder expectations.
The enterprise shall obtain MDR/SDR acceptance at the end of Phase A for a credible EPS architecture with requirement allocations and justified alternatives.

The enterprise shall obtain PDR acceptance at the end of Phase B for a sized, compatible preliminary EPS design supported by sizing and trades, margins, risk dispositions, controlled interfaces and verification and validation plans against applicable requirements and agreed technical resource and risk limits.

The enterprise shall obtain scoped CDR acceptance during adapted Phase C, before deliverable coding, for complete detailed EPS model and software designs, interface specifications and implementation, integration and verification and validation plans.

The enterprise shall obtain scoped SIR acceptance at the end of adapted Phase C for released EPS models and declared control and interface software for host execution, applicable MIL/SIL evidence, compatible interfaces and ready integration configurations and procedures.

framework_requirements.text: The framework shall retain each requirement with its identifier, revision, statement, product level, source and parent revisions, rationale, owner, conditions or quantities, applicable units, verification method, criterion and resolution status, including reasons for unresolved or inapplicable fields.
framework_requirements.inputs: Requirement submissions and source/parent revisions.
framework_requirements.outputs: Retained requirement records and field resolution status.
framework_requirements.rationale: Retained metadata and rationale preserve requirement intent, ownership, derivation and verification context \citep[Table~4.2-2, p.~60]{nasa2016systems} \citep[Sec.~IV.B]{review-1438}.

framework_requirements.text: The framework shall check created or edited requirement drafts on each edit or request for declared deterministic quality errors, probable semantic duplicates, coverage gaps and source conflicts, returning affected text or records, the rule or cited passage, corrective suggestions or questions, uncertainty and assessment limits.
framework_requirements.inputs: Draft edits/requests, current requirements, rules, sources and coverage references.
framework_requirements.outputs: Explained findings, corrections/questions and assessment limits.
framework_requirements.rationale: Explained draft checks expose ambiguity, omissions, redundancy and inconsistency before requirement acceptance \citep[Sec.~4.2.1.2.4, Appendix~C]{nasa2016systems} \citep[Sec.~II]{review-1438}.

framework_requirements.text: The framework shall recommend derivation, analysis, verification and validation methods or models on edits or requests using the current lifecycle stage, engineering question, requirements, available inputs, validity, resources and scope, with applicability conditions, rationale, cited sources, alternatives and rejection records.
framework_requirements.inputs: Current phase/question, requirements, inputs, validity, resources and scope.
framework_requirements.outputs: Cited method/model recommendations, alternatives and rejection records.
framework_requirements.rationale: Phase and input constraints determine which EPS sizing, simulation and assessment methods are suitable \citep[Secs.~2--4]{handpicked-0003} \citep[Sec.~6.8.1.2]{nasa2016systems}.

framework_requirements.text: The framework shall retrieve forward and reverse links among expectations, ConOps scenarios, requirements, function and element allocations, interfaces, decisions and applicable evidence, reporting missing or ambiguous endpoints and coverage against the declared reference set.
framework_requirements.inputs: Trace query, linked records and declared reference set.
framework_requirements.outputs: Forward/reverse links, endpoint gaps and coverage.
framework_requirements.rationale: Explicit links reveal requirement coverage and gaps across scenarios, allocations, interfaces and verification evidence \citep[Sec.~6.2.1.2]{nasa2016systems} \citep[Secs.~IV.H--I]{review-1438}.

framework_requirements.text: The framework shall identify reciprocal impacts of a proposed mission, requirement, component, interface, model or software change on EPS/non-EPS allocations, budgets, trades, plans, guidance and evidence, reporting unresolved dependencies and required reassessments.
framework_requirements.inputs: Proposed change and current engineering dependencies.
framework_requirements.outputs: Reciprocal impacts, unresolved dependencies and required reassessments.
framework_requirements.rationale: Dependency links expose reciprocal EPS and spacecraft impacts and guide necessary reassessment after changes. \citep[Secs.~III.C and~IV]{review-0764} \citep[Sec.~III.C]{cordero2022nanospace}

framework_requirements.text: The framework shall issue a distinct successor baseline only for an authorized engineering change decision, preserving its predecessor, request, rationale, findings and dispositions and identifying regenerated, stale and unresolved products and evidence.
framework_requirements.inputs: Predecessor baseline, change request and authorized change acceptance.
framework_requirements.outputs: Successor baseline, preserved predecessor and product/evidence status.
framework_requirements.rationale: Authorized changes preserve the prior engineering basis and make revised product and evidence status explicit. \citep[Sec.~2, RQ-3]{kanavouras2024lightweight} \citep[Sec.~6.5.1.2.3]{nasa2016systems}

framework_requirements.text: The framework shall retain retrievable phase baselines that resolve exact requirement, mission, design, model, software, interface and evidence revisions with revision history and the authorized decisions that control them.
framework_requirements.inputs: Product/evidence revisions, decisions and baseline retrieval request.
framework_requirements.outputs: Retrievable exact baselines and revision/decision histories.
framework_requirements.rationale: Retrievable version histories establish the exact engineering basis used for phase decisions and evidence. \citep[Sec.~2, RQ-3]{kanavouras2024lightweight} \citep[Sec.~6.5.1.2.4]{nasa2016systems}

framework_requirements.text: The framework shall check transferred identities, revisions, structure, quantities, units, polarity, time/mode meanings and provenance against the declared interface specification before registration, retaining incompatible raw submissions and findings without replacing controlled content.
framework_requirements.inputs: Raw submissions and declared interface specification.
framework_requirements.outputs: Admitted transfers or retained rejections with unchanged controlled content.
framework_requirements.rationale: Declared meanings and tool specific structures govern compatible exchanges of EPS engineering data. \citep[Sec.~3.3]{review-1277} \citep[Sec.~3.3]{luccisano2024formalization}

framework_requirements.text: The framework shall associate each analysis or software result with its requirement/expectation, method, scenario, design/model/software/input revisions, parameters, producer, execution environment, raw outputs, logs and execution status, preserving failed, cancelled and partial runs.
framework_requirements.inputs: Analysis/software results, exact dependencies, logs and status.
framework_requirements.outputs: Configuration-linked results, provenance and execution status.
framework_requirements.rationale: Configuration linked results preserve the scenario, method and evidence basis of EPS conclusions. \citep[Sec.~6.2.3]{handpicked-0003} \citep[Sec.~5.3.1.2.4]{nasa2016systems}

framework_requirements.text: The framework shall provide the controlled inputs, dependencies and instructions to reconstruct a designated analysis or MIL/SIL run and compare its raw outputs using result-specific rules and tolerances fixed before replay, retaining comparison failures and missing dependencies.
framework_requirements.inputs: Replay request, preserved run/dependencies, returned outputs and fixed comparison rules.
framework_requirements.outputs: Replay inputs/instructions, comparisons and dependency/failure findings.
framework_requirements.rationale: Preserved inputs, procedures and comparison criteria make repeated assessments comparable and expose reconstruction gaps. \citep[Secs.~III.B--III.C]{cordero2022nanospace} \citep[Table~5.3-1]{nasa2016systems}

framework_requirements.text: The framework shall report missing, rejected, stale, failed, out-of-domain and unresolved evidence against the affected requirements, expectations and conclusions with criticality, owner and disposition, preventing unqualified current conformity claims from affected critical gaps.
framework_requirements.inputs: Evidence/status, affected requirements/expectations and criticality rules.
framework_requirements.outputs: Gap reports and blocked unsupported conformity claims.
framework_requirements.rationale: Explicit evidence gaps keep EPS conformity conclusions within the scope of completed, applicable assessments. \citep[Sec.~8.2]{handpicked-0003} \citep[Secs.~5.3.1.2.3 and~5.3.1.3]{nasa2016systems}

framework_requirements.text: The framework shall calculate revision-linked EPS mass and volume estimates from modeled component and design data, retaining sources, units, aggregation assumptions, uncertainty and unknown values.
framework_requirements.inputs: Modeled component and design data with sourced mass and volume properties.
framework_requirements.outputs: Mass and volume estimates with uncertainty and unknowns.
framework_requirements.rationale: Component aggregation and margins expose whether EPS designs fit spacecraft mass and volume limits \citep[Sec.~3 and Table~4]{handpicked-0003} \citep[Secs.~2 and~3.2.2]{luccisano2024formalization}.

framework_requirements.text: The framework shall compare designated EPS concepts and architectures on common requirements, mission assumptions and engineer-approved criteria, separating mandatory feasibility from preference ranking and reporting raw measures, margins, uncertainty, sensitivity, risks and selection rationale.
framework_requirements.inputs: EPS alternatives, common mission/requirements and approved criteria.
framework_requirements.outputs: Feasibility, ranking, sensitivity and selection rationale.
framework_requirements.rationale: Feasibility screening and transparent criteria make EPS architecture choices reviewable under uncertainty \citep[Sec.~4]{handpicked-0003} \citep[Sec.~6.8.1.2]{nasa2016systems}.

framework_requirements.text: The framework shall configure EPS design representations through identified parameters, component variants and extensions covering generation, storage, conversion, regulation, protection, distribution, control, interfaces and requirement allocations.
framework_requirements.inputs: Design parameters, component variants, extensions and allocations.
framework_requirements.outputs: Configured EPS design representations.
framework_requirements.rationale: Mission requirements drive configurable EPS architectures, component parameters, protection functions and subsystem interfaces \citep[Secs.~4 and~7]{handpicked-0003} \citep[Sec.~3.2]{luccisano2024formalization}.

framework_requirements.text: The framework shall compose time-dependent subsystem loads, schedules and mode transitions with orbit, attitude, illumination, eclipse, thermal conditions and modeled EPS generation, storage, losses and protection to report power/energy balance, bus quantities and battery state within the declared model scope.
framework_requirements.inputs: Whole-CUBICS mission/subsystem load and mode histories, orbit/attitude/illumination/thermal histories and EPS models.
framework_requirements.outputs: Power/energy balance, bus quantities and battery state histories.
framework_requirements.rationale: Mission modes, attitude and eclipse jointly determine EPS demand, generation and battery discharge \citep[Secs.~2--3 and~6.2.3]{handpicked-0003}.

framework_requirements.text: The framework shall produce proposed EPS and component requirement allocations from identified spacecraft requirements, scenarios and sourced design quantities using a declared derivation method, retaining parent links, units, assumptions, uncertainty and engineer dispositions.
framework_requirements.inputs: Spacecraft requirements, scenarios, quantities and derivation method.
framework_requirements.outputs: Proposed EPS/component allocations, traces and dispositions.
framework_requirements.rationale: Mission loads and operating scenarios determine traceable EPS generation, storage and component requirement allocations \citep[Secs.~3 and~7]{handpicked-0003} \citep[Sec.~4.3.1.2.2]{nasa2016systems}.

framework_requirements.text: The framework shall exchange identified component and design models through declared electrical, thermal, applicable EMC and geometry profiles and couple EPS analyses to the required NVIDIA Omniverse whole-CUBICS simulation. The coupling shall receive spacecraft and subsystem scenario inputs and return EPS states and results under declared directions, entity/channel mappings, quantities and units, model/tool revisions, supported effects, execution status and unsupported or lossy transfers.
framework_requirements.inputs: Component/design model revisions, discipline and Omniverse coupling profiles, whole-CUBICS model/scenario revisions, spacecraft/subsystem scenario histories, directed mappings and returned tool responses.
framework_requirements.outputs: Exchanged component/design models, mapped EPS analysis inputs, EPS states/results returned to the same whole-CUBICS scenario, mapping findings, execution status and transfer limitations.
framework_requirements.rationale: EPS compatibility requires consistent discipline exchanges and explicit mappings between scenario inputs and numerical outputs \citep[Sec.~7.7]{handpicked-0003}\citep[pp.~4--5]{handpicked-0001}.

framework_requirements.text: The framework shall coordinate MIL assessment of modeled EPS control against the plant and mission scenarios for nominal operation, load/supply changes, mode transitions, selected faults, protection and recovery, retaining stimuli, expected/actual responses, criteria and failures.
framework_requirements.inputs: Controller/plant models, mission scenarios and MIL criteria.
framework_requirements.outputs: MIL requests, retained stimuli/responses and criterion outcomes/failures.
framework_requirements.rationale: Exercise modeled EPS control under changing supply, loads and faults before host software integration \citep[Secs.~2.2 and~4]{review-0573} \citep[Sec.~8.1.6]{handpicked-0003}.

framework_requirements.text: The framework shall calculate preliminary generation, demand and energy budgets and array/battery sizing for the declared mission modes, including sourced efficiencies, duty cycles, eclipse duration, allowable battery operating limits, degradation assumptions and engineer-defined margins.
framework_requirements.inputs: Mission modes/loads, efficiencies, duty cycles, eclipse, battery limits, degradation and margins.
framework_requirements.outputs: Power/energy budgets and array/battery sizing.
framework_requirements.rationale: Mission loads, eclipses, efficiencies and degradation determine array and battery sizing and required margins \citep[Secs.~3 and~6.2]{handpicked-0003}.

framework_requirements.text: The framework shall associate each model-supported conclusion with intended use, selected fidelity, included and omitted mechanisms, numerical checks, validity domain, uncertainty, calibration evidence and independent assessment evidence or explicit gaps, with engineer-approved prediction-error rules.
framework_requirements.inputs: Conclusions, model scope, credibility evidence and error rules.
framework_requirements.outputs: Conclusion-linked credibility records and explicit gaps.
framework_requirements.rationale: EPS predictions require declared model scope, assessed assumptions and evidence appropriate to their intended use \citep[Secs.~2.2.3--2.2.4]{friedenthal2014practical}\citep[Secs.~7.7 and~8.2]{handpicked-0003}.

framework_requirements.text: The framework shall propose identified model calibration or parameter revisions from quality-checked supplied reference data, retaining prior/revised values, data revisions, residuals, uncertainty and affected analyses separately from independent model assessment.
framework_requirements.inputs: Current parameters and quality-checked supplied reference data.
framework_requirements.outputs: Calibration proposals, residuals, uncertainty and affected analyses.
framework_requirements.rationale: EPS assessment needs reference comparisons \citep[Sec.~8.1.6]{handpicked-0003} and documented calibration distinct from prediction assessment \citep[Sec.~4.1]{review-1251}.

framework_requirements.text: The framework shall retain the fidelity, solver and coupling configuration, time step, convergence rules, execution environment, required resources and estimated/measured runtime for each analysis, MIL or SIL run, with unmet resource or numerical limits reported.
framework_requirements.inputs: Run settings, environment, resource limits and observations.
framework_requirements.outputs: Run configuration/runtime records and numerical/resource findings.
framework_requirements.rationale: Numerical results depend on declared execution settings, temporal resolution and available computing resources \citep[Sec.~6.2.3]{handpicked-0003}\citep[Sec.~3, Table~3]{review-0573}.

framework_requirements.text: The framework shall coordinate SIL assessment of released F Prime host-executed EPS control/interface software with simulated EPS and subsystem products connected to NVIDIA Omniverse whole-CUBICS simulation, reporting requirement/ConOps outcomes and differences from corresponding MIL results for the same scenarios and comparison rules.
framework_requirements.inputs: Released F Prime host code/build, simulated EPS/subsystem products, whole-CUBICS scenario and coupling-profile revisions, matched MIL results and fixed comparison rules.
framework_requirements.outputs: SIL requests, retained host responses, requirement/ConOps outcomes and MIL/SIL differences with execution status and limits.
framework_requirements.rationale: Compare host software responses with modeled EPS behavior under common scenarios before integration acceptance \citep[p.~3]{handpicked-0001} \citep[Sec.~8.1.7]{handpicked-0003}.

framework_requirements.text: The framework shall retain mission expectations, constraints and nominal/degraded ConOps scenarios with orbit, attitude, duration, environmental conditions, subsystem modes, load schedules and transitions as revision-linked inputs to EPS requirements and analysis.
framework_requirements.inputs: Mission expectations, constraints and nominal/degraded ConOps.
framework_requirements.outputs: Revision-linked mission and ConOps records.
framework_requirements.rationale: Mission conditions and operating modes determine EPS requirements, load profiles and energy availability \citep[Secs.~2 and~6.1]{handpicked-0003} \citep[Appendix~S, Secs.~3.4,~4 and~6]{nasa2016systems}.

framework_requirements.text: The framework shall identify reliability, availability and maintainability analyses applicable to the designated EPS requirements, ConOps and risks, retaining the chosen measures, failure/repair assumptions, method coverage and reasons for exclusions.
framework_requirements.inputs: EPS requirements, ConOps, risks and failure/repair assumptions.
framework_requirements.outputs: Applicable RAM methods, measures, coverage and exclusions.
framework_requirements.rationale: RAM method choice depends on mission risks, design maturity, failure dependencies and available evidence \citep[Secs.~4--5]{handpicked-0003}\citep[Secs.~4 and~6]{review-0913}.

framework_requirements.text: The framework shall generate the selected RAM analysis representation from identified functions, components and failure dependencies using declared transformation rules, preserving sourced or missing failure/repair data and uncertainty in the reported results.
framework_requirements.inputs: Functions, components, failure dependencies, data and transformation rules.
framework_requirements.outputs: RAM representations/results with uncertainty and missing data.
framework_requirements.rationale: EPS fault dependencies need assessment \citep[Sec.~7.1]{handpicked-0003}. Declared RAM transformations preserve traceability and expose data gaps and uncertainty \citep[Sec.~V.B, p.~15]{handpicked-0004}.

framework_requirements.text: The framework shall retain EPS phase-product verification and validation plans with distinct requirement and expectation/ConOps references, subject configuration, method, conditions, inputs, expected response, criteria, observations, applicability limits and planned/executed status.
framework_requirements.inputs: EPS requirements/expectations, assessment plans and observations.
framework_requirements.outputs: Retained EPS V\&V plans, separate references and planned/executed status.
framework_requirements.rationale: Distinct verification and validation links preserve EPS assessment intent, criteria and execution status. \citep[Sec.~5]{handpicked-0003} \citep[pp.~5--6]{kaslow2019csrm}

framework_requirements.text: The framework shall retain the authorized engineer disposition of each requirement correction or method/model suggestion as accepted, modified, rejected or deferred, with rationale and the exact suggestion and context revisions.
framework_requirements.inputs: Suggestion/context revisions and authorized engineer decision.
framework_requirements.outputs: Recorded disposition, rationale and revision links.
framework_requirements.rationale: Recorded engineer decisions preserve accountability and the rationale for accepting or declining proposed guidance \citep[Sec.~6.8.1]{nasa2016systems} \citep[Sec.~1]{review-0711}.

framework_requirements.text: The framework shall mark affected assistance stale when its requirement, mission, design, source, criterion or scope revision changes, prevent stale suggestions from being applied as current guidance and initiate reassessment for the new context.
framework_requirements.inputs: Changed context revisions and affected assistance.
framework_requirements.outputs: Stale status, blocked application and reassessment request.
framework_requirements.rationale: Changed context requires affected guidance to be reassessed before it supports current engineering decisions \citep[Secs.~6.2.1.2.4--5]{nasa2016systems} \citep[Sec.~III.C]{review-0764}.

framework_requirements.text: The framework shall retain and check scenario time bases, sample and receipt times, sampling, synchronization and known calculation/interface delays for simulated or supplied reference histories, including coupled exchanges, against declared timing rules, reporting missing timing data and exceeded synchronization limits.
framework_requirements.inputs: Exchanged/simulated/reference histories, scenario time references, sampling/exchange timing, synchronization rules and limits, and known delays.
framework_requirements.outputs: Timing and synchronization records, checked alignments, timing gaps and limit findings.
framework_requirements.rationale: Time alignment and known delays govern whether coupled EPS histories support meaningful comparisons \citep[Sec.~8.1.7]{handpicked-0003}\citep[Sec.~3, Table~3]{review-0573}.

framework_requirements.text: The framework shall check exchanged, simulated and supplied reference histories for entity/channel identity, units, timing, completeness and validity before numerical use, preserving raw values, invalid samples, missing intervals and processing masks without treating missing or inactive readings as zero.
framework_requirements.inputs: Exchanged/simulated/reference histories, entity/channel mappings, quantity/unit definitions, timing metadata and validity rules.
framework_requirements.outputs: Admission/quality findings, preserved raw histories, invalid/missing/inactive status and processing masks.
framework_requirements.rationale: Validity checks and channel mappings prevent inactive or missing readings from distorting EPS calculations \citep[Sec.~4.2]{review-1251}\citep[Sec.~8.1.7]{handpicked-0003}.

framework_requirements.text: The framework shall retain revision-linked modeled EPS interfaces and command, telemetry, event and parameter definitions with endpoint ownership, directions, identifiers, types, units, ranges, polarity, time/mode meaning and encodings.
framework_requirements.inputs: Modeled EPS endpoint/port interfaces and command, telemetry, event and parameter definitions.
framework_requirements.outputs: Revision-linked EPS interface and ground-definition specifications.
framework_requirements.rationale: Preserve consistent EPS interface and ground meanings as designs mature toward host integration \citep[Secs.~7.2 and~8.1.7]{handpicked-0003} \citep[Table~5, p.~12]{review-0853}.

framework_requirements.text: The framework shall produce or coordinate checked mappings of the EPS interface specification to the required versioned F Prime host integration profile, covering component, port, topology, command, telemetry, event and parameter definitions and identifying version compatibility, unsupported behavior and lossy translations.
framework_requirements.inputs: EPS interface specification, software component/instance ownership and connectivity, required F Prime profile and supported representation/tool versions.
framework_requirements.outputs: Checked F Prime mappings and definitions, compatibility findings and unsupported/lossy-translation records.
framework_requirements.rationale: Expose translation limits and preserve modeled architecture and separately supplied ground definitions in F Prime \citep[Sec.~3, p.~7 and Table~5, ArchGen-2]{review-0853}.

framework_requirements.text: The framework shall specify and check modeled EPS command preconditions, order, effects, rejection/failure behavior, mode transitions, protection and recovery responsibilities against the declared control and interface requirements.
framework_requirements.inputs: Modeled command/control behavior and control/interface requirements.
framework_requirements.outputs: Checked behavior specifications and discrepancy findings.
framework_requirements.rationale: Make command conditions, mode transitions, protection and recovery responsibilities explicit before verification \citep[Secs.~7.4--7.5 and~8.1.6]{handpicked-0003} \citep[Table~5, FuncDev-2]{review-0853}.

framework_requirements.text: The framework shall coordinate coding and host building of declared F Prime EPS control/interface flight software through an external toolchain only from a current engineer-authorized detailed design release, retaining source/build revisions, toolchain versions, dependencies, host configuration, logs and failures.
framework_requirements.inputs: Current authorized design/interface release, declared software scope, F Prime mappings, host/toolchain/dependency configuration and returned tool responses.
framework_requirements.outputs: Authorized coding/build requests, retained source/build products, exact configuration records, logs and failures.
framework_requirements.rationale: Tie mission-specific F Prime coding and builds to approved detailed designs and identifiable configurations \citep[Sec.~3.6, p.~29]{nasa2016systems} \citep[Table~5, ArchGen-3 and FuncDev-5--6]{review-0853}.

framework_requirements.text: The framework shall generate filtered mission, requirement-allocation, design, interface and analysis views from controlled EPS records with baseline identification, readable units, legends and links to represented records.
framework_requirements.inputs: Controlled EPS baseline and view selection.
framework_requirements.outputs: Readable baseline-linked engineering views.
framework_requirements.rationale: Model derived views communicate EPS requirements, interfaces and analysis while preserving their shared engineering basis. \citep[Sec.~IV]{review-0764} \citep[Sec.~4.2]{chiu2023sealion}

framework_requirements.text: The framework shall assemble a phase-baseline review package against the designated MCR, SRR, MDR/SDR, PDR, scoped CDR or scoped SIR entrance and success criteria, including applicable coverage, decisions, design, evidence, model limits, risks, gaps and finding dispositions.
framework_requirements.inputs: Phase baseline, review criteria and applicable records/evidence.
framework_requirements.outputs: Prepared review package with coverage, limits and findings.
framework_requirements.rationale: Baseline linked design and evidence packages let reviewers assess phase criteria, risks and unresolved findings. \citep[pp.~4--5]{kaslow2019csrm} \citep[Sec.~6.7, Table~6.7-1]{nasa2016systems}

framework_requirements.text: The framework shall propose next engineering activities and repeated assessments from the declared phase, product maturity, dependencies, open findings and review criteria, identifying unmet prerequisites and the rationale for each proposal.

Close all prior conditions, then submit a renewed conditional decision with complete new conditions and no blockers. Repeat renewals with stale/unauthorized decisions, missing prior closure evidence and incomplete new conditional records.
verification_cases.expected_response: Record only admitted designated-authority dispositions. Separate prepared/accepted/conditional/blocked, with rationale/conditions/actions/owners/dates. Renewed acceptance requires an explicit accepted decision, completed prior closure evidence and no blockers. A renewed conditional decision remains conditional even after prior conditions close. A renewed blocked decision records progression-blocked status and never acceptance.
verification_cases.criteria_comparison_basis: Exact reference authority, baseline, criteria, decision disposition and state-transition agreement. Prior-condition closure evidence cannot override the renewed disposition. Inconsistent or incomplete decisions remain rejected and alter no progression.
verification_cases.retained_evidence: Packages/findings, initial and renewed decision records, separate prior-condition closure evidence, authority/context checks and state histories, exact subject/environment/reference versions, as-run procedure, deviations, discrepancy dispositions and planned reruns

mission_requirements.text: The EPS engineering enterprise shall obtain MCR acceptance at the end of Pre-Phase A for a mission concept whose EPS feasibility is justified against agreed stakeholder expectations and mission constraints, supported by initial ConOps, budgets, assumptions, risks and a preliminary verification and validation approach.

The enterprise shall obtain SRR acceptance during Phase A for validated EPS requirements and interfaces traced to the mission concept and allocated spacecraft requirements, with measurable criteria consistent with stakeholder expectations. It shall derive, refine and validate EPS and component requirements and interfaces as the design matures through Phase B and adapted C.

The enterprise shall obtain MDR/SDR acceptance at the end of Phase A for a credible EPS architecture with requirement allocations and justified alternatives, and PDR acceptance at the end of Phase B for a sized, compatible preliminary design supported by sizing and trades, margins, risk dispositions, controlled interfaces and verification and validation plans against applicable requirements and agreed resource and risk limits.

The enterprise shall obtain CDR acceptance during adapted Phase C, before deliverable coding, for complete detailed EPS model/software design, interface specifications and implementation, integration and verification and validation plans, followed by SIR acceptance at the end of C for released models and declared host-executed control/interface software, applicable MIL/SIL evidence, compatible interfaces and ready integration configurations and procedures.

The enterprise shall establish and maintain coherent phase baselines through authorized changes, repeated affected checks and applicable verification and validation evidence, retaining configuration-linked requirements, expectations, methods, results, limitations and finding dispositions. It shall obtain and retain acceptance decisions from the designated review authority against agreed success criteria, prevent progression with blocking findings, and record conditional limits, closure actions, owners and dates.

framework_requirements.text: The framework shall retain each requirement with its identifier, revision, statement, product level, source and parent revisions, rationale, owner, conditions or quantities, applicable units, verification method, criterion and resolution status, including reasons for unresolved or inapplicable fields.

The framework shall check created or edited requirement drafts on each edit or request for declared deterministic quality errors, probable semantic duplicates, coverage gaps and source conflicts, returning affected text or records, the rule or cited passage, corrective suggestions or questions, uncertainty and assessment limits.

The framework shall recommend derivation, analysis, verification and validation methods or models on edits or requests using the current lifecycle stage, engineering question, requirements, available inputs, validity, resources and scope, with applicability conditions, rationale, cited sources, alternatives and rejection records.

The framework shall retrieve forward and reverse links among expectations, ConOps scenarios, requirements, function and element allocations, interfaces, decisions and applicable evidence, reporting missing or ambiguous endpoints and coverage against the declared reference set.

The framework shall identify reciprocal impacts of a proposed mission, requirement, component, interface, model or software change on EPS/non-EPS allocations, budgets, trades, plans, guidance and evidence, reporting unresolved dependencies and required reassessments.

The framework shall issue a distinct successor baseline only for an authorized engineering change decision, preserving its predecessor, request, rationale, findings and dispositions and identifying regenerated, stale and unresolved products and evidence.

The framework shall retain retrievable phase baselines that resolve exact requirement, mission, design, model, software, interface and evidence revisions with revision history and the authorized decisions that control them.

The framework shall check transferred identities, revisions, structure, quantities, units, polarity, time/mode meanings and provenance against the declared interface specification before registration, retaining incompatible raw submissions and findings without replacing controlled content.

The framework shall associate each analysis or software result with its requirement/expectation, method, scenario, design/model/software/input revisions, parameters, producer, execution environment, raw outputs, logs and execution status, preserving failed, cancelled and partial runs.

The framework shall provide the controlled inputs, dependencies and instructions to reconstruct a designated analysis or MIL/SIL run and compare its raw outputs using result-specific rules and tolerances fixed before replay, retaining comparison failures and missing dependencies.

The framework shall report missing, rejected, stale, failed, out-of-domain and unresolved evidence against the affected requirements, expectations and conclusions with criticality, owner and disposition, preventing unqualified current conformity claims from affected critical gaps.

The framework shall generate and revise candidate-specific bills of materials from modeled design occurrences with assembly relationships, quantities, part and variant identifiers, source revisions and selection status.

The framework shall calculate revision-linked EPS mass, volume and acquisition-cost estimates from the bill of materials and declared additional categories, retaining sources, price dates, currencies, availability assumptions, uncertainty and unknown values.

The framework shall compare designated EPS concepts and architectures on common requirements, mission assumptions and engineer-approved criteria, separating mandatory feasibility from preference ranking and reporting raw measures, margins, uncertainty, sensitivity, risks and selection rationale.

The framework shall configure EPS design representations through identified parameters, component variants and extensions covering generation, storage, conversion, regulation, protection, distribution, control, interfaces and requirement allocations.

The framework shall compose time-dependent subsystem loads, schedules and mode transitions with orbit, attitude, illumination, eclipse, thermal conditions and modeled EPS generation, storage, losses and protection to report power/energy balance, bus quantities and battery state within the declared model scope.

The framework shall produce proposed EPS and component requirement allocations from identified spacecraft requirements, scenarios and sourced design quantities using a declared derivation method, retaining parent links, units, assumptions, uncertainty and engineer dispositions.

The framework shall exchange identified component and design models with declared electrical, thermal, applicable EMC and geometry analysis profiles, retaining input/output mappings, tool versions, units, supported effects and unsupported or lossy transfers.

The framework shall coordinate MIL assessment of modeled EPS control against the plant and mission scenarios for nominal operation, load/supply changes, mode transitions, selected faults, protection and recovery, retaining stimuli, expected/actual responses, criteria and failures.

The framework shall calculate preliminary generation, demand and energy budgets and array/battery sizing for the declared mission modes, including sourced efficiencies, duty cycles, eclipse duration, allowable battery operating limits, degradation assumptions and engineer-defined margins.

The framework shall associate each model-supported conclusion with intended use, selected fidelity, included and omitted mechanisms, numerical checks, validity domain, uncertainty, calibration evidence and independent assessment evidence or explicit gaps, with engineer-approved prediction-error rules.

The framework shall propose identified model calibration or parameter revisions from quality-checked supplied reference data, retaining prior/revised values, data revisions, residuals, uncertainty and affected analyses separately from independent model assessment.

The framework shall retain the fidelity, solver and coupling configuration, time step, convergence rules, execution environment, required resources and estimated/measured runtime for each analysis, MIL or SIL run, with unmet resource or numerical limits reported.

The framework shall coordinate SIL assessment of the declared host-executed control/interface code with simulated EPS and subsystem products, reporting requirement/ConOps outcomes and differences from corresponding MIL results for the same scenarios and comparison rules.

The framework shall retain mission expectations, constraints and nominal/degraded ConOps scenarios with orbit, attitude, duration, environmental conditions, subsystem modes, load schedules and transitions as revision-linked inputs to EPS requirements and analysis.

The framework shall identify reliability, availability and maintainability analyses applicable to the designated EPS requirements, ConOps and risks, retaining the chosen measures, failure/repair assumptions, method coverage and reasons for exclusions.

The framework shall generate the selected RAM analysis representation from identified functions, components and failure dependencies using declared transformation rules, preserving sourced or missing failure/repair data and uncertainty in the reported results.

The framework shall retain EPS phase-product verification and validation plans with distinct requirement and expectation/ConOps references, subject configuration, method, conditions, inputs, expected response, criteria, observations, applicability limits and planned/executed status.

The framework shall retain the authorized engineer disposition of each requirement correction or method/model suggestion as accepted, modified, rejected or deferred, with rationale and the exact suggestion and context revisions.

The framework shall mark affected assistance stale when its requirement, mission, design, source, criterion or scope revision changes, prevent stale suggestions from being applied as current guidance and initiate reassessment for the new context.

The framework shall retain scenario time bases, sample and receipt times, sampling, synchronization and known calculation/interface delays for simulated or supplied reference histories used in comparisons.

The framework shall check simulated and supplied reference histories for channel identity, units, timing, completeness and validity, preserving raw values, invalid samples, missing intervals and processing masks without treating missing or inactive readings as zero.

The framework shall retain revision-linked modeled EPS interfaces and command, telemetry, event and parameter definitions with endpoint ownership, identifiers, types, units, ranges, polarity, time/mode meaning and encodings.

The framework shall produce or coordinate checked mappings of the EPS interface specification to the engineer-selected host software integration profile, identifying version compatibility, unsupported behavior and lossy translations.

The framework shall specify and check modeled EPS command preconditions, order, effects, rejection/failure behavior, mode transitions, protection and recovery responsibilities against the declared control and interface requirements.

The framework shall coordinate coding and building of declared control/interface software through an external host execution toolchain only from an engineer-authorized detailed design release, retaining source/build revisions, dependencies, host configuration, logs and failures.

The framework shall generate filtered mission, requirement-allocation, design, interface and analysis views from controlled EPS records with baseline identification, readable units, legends and links to represented records.

The framework shall assemble a phase-baseline review package against the designated MCR, SRR, MDR/SDR, PDR, scoped CDR or scoped SIR entrance and success criteria, including applicable coverage, decisions, design, evidence, model limits, risks, gaps and finding dispositions.

The framework shall propose next engineering activities and repeated assessments from the declared phase, product maturity, dependencies, open findings and review criteria, identifying unmet prerequisites and the rationale for each proposal.

The framework shall acknowledge each assistance trigger and return a finding, recommendation or explicit pending/unavailable status within the engineer-approved interactive response limits, recording trigger, first-response and completion times for the current context.

The framework shall record a technical review disposition only from the designated authorized review authority against the identified baseline and agreed scoped success criteria, distinguishing prepared, accepted, conditional and progression-blocked status with rationale, conditions, closure actions, owners and dates.

measures_of_effectiveness.observation_basis: Engineering burden: active person-hours and elapsed hours for correct requirements, design, change and review tasks, with waiting and unattended execution reported separately.
Early issue detection: expert-confirmed issues found before scoped final design, critical misses and unnecessary investigations against a declared reference issue set.
Evidence and review usefulness: applicable requirement and expectation coverage, critical review defects, reviewer interpretation accuracy and successful independent reconstruction.
Adoption and affordability: person-hours to learn and complete correct tasks and adapt to a mission, and direct framework usage cost in CAD over a declared period and price date.

measures_of_performance.observation_basis: Trigger-to-acknowledgement, first current answer and completion percentiles, outages and superseded edits
Deterministic agreement, semantic precision/recall, critical misses, false positives, abstention, explanation/source correctness and recommendation eligibility/ranking
Budget/sizing and transfer agreement, numerical convergence, validity violations and runtime for a declared workload
Impact precision/recall and stale or unauthorized outputs presented as current, including interrupted changes
Applicable reconstruction success and raw-output agreement under rules fixed before replay, including missing dependencies
Review interpretation accuracy, required package omissions, correct task completion and declared-host resource footprint
